blocks.text: Katie Dill, Head of Design at Stripe, makes a helpful comparison. Under pressure to build quickly after World War II, builders copied the clean shapes and bare surfaces of modernism over and over. The copies kept the look while losing the thought and character behind it. Her warning is that AI can do the same to software. She calls it “zombie UI” and says we need a point of view, because “if you don’t, AI will give it for you.”

HyperFrames for editing:
HyperFrames
, HeyGen's open-source video framework, turns a video into a web page. Clips, screen recordings, captions and text are just elements on that page, and a
GSAP

timeline moves them around. So when someone asks to caption a webinar or cut a product demo, the agent edits it like a web page. Its CLI is basically the agent's editing suite: lint the composition, pull a frame to check, render the cut. We also install

motion-studio
for animation:

A web page can't blur fast motion, make things glow or turn a logo in 3D, and that's the finish we wanted for original animation. So we built our own canvas engine. The agent writes code that draws every pixel of every frame, and the engine blends up to 16 moments into each one, the same way a camera shutter blurs movement. The parrot film was made this way.

blocks.text: Motion is especially expensive to get wrong, both in render time and tokens. A storyboard frame takes about 50 milliseconds to render, compared to 8 to 40 seconds for a single second of finished film. blocks.text: Remember those early reviews? The biggest improvement came from capturing our designers’ judgment in a shared environment the agent could learn from, rather than leaving it scattered across review threads. In the process, we made design work accessible to more people.

blocks.text: Next, we want the agent to manage the entire campaign lifecycle, and some of that is already working. It publishes company social posts through Buffer once an authorized approver signs off, drafts posts for employees to share from their own accounts, and runs scheduled routines, including a daily review that suggests posts worth quoting.

blocks.text: Our goal is to take this further, so a single approved creative direction can carry an entire campaign from one thread. The agent would write the brief, create assets for each channel, schedule posts, help the team amplify them, and use performance data to inform the next campaign. People would still review and approve everything before it goes public.
